title: Annotatio IV §.II: First fountain — free-acting pravity of will precedes intellect-error; sacred strife by free choice
pass_a_gloss: Of the two Fountains, the Prior is the free-acting Pravity of Will, which no less under the Covenant of Grace than of Works precedes the error of Intellect: since even the nature of any divine Covenant begun with man presupposes so much Light in the human intellect as suffices for the malicious Pravity of will either to be restrained or repelled, so that one who has advanced to sacred quarrels and Ecclesiastical dissensions beyond necessity, even with the Devil instigating, may know that he has rushed into the same not unwillingly, or through intellect’s error, or through the Devil’s persuasion, but rather through his own free election and προαίρεσις — three greater rivulets promoting the business of dissensions, flowing from the will’s pravity and well noted by the Apostle John, being here to be recounted in inverse order:
pass_b_english: Of the two fountains, the first is the free-acting pravity of the will — which, under the covenant of grace no less than of works, runs ahead of intellect’s error.
For any divine covenant with man presupposes enough light in the mind to restrain or repel malicious will-pravity.

So whoever has gone on to needless sacred quarrels and church splits — even with the Devil prodding — should know he rushed in not unwillingly, nor merely by intellect’s mistake or the Devil’s talk, but by his own free choice and προαίρεσις.
Three larger rivulets from will-pravity, well marked by the Apostle John, promote that work of dissension; we list them here in reverse order:
source_text: Fontium binorum Priorem, Pravitatem Voluntatis facio-liberam, non minus sub Foedere Gratiae, quam Operum, errorem Intellectûs praevertentem: cum vel ipsius Foederis divini cujuscunque cum homine initi natura, tantum Luminis in intellectu humano supponat, quantum sufficit Pravitati voluntatis malitiosae vel cohibendae, vel repellendae, ut sic ad rixas sacras & dissidia Ecclesiastica praeter necessitatem, etiamsi instigante Diabolo, progressus, sciat, se non invitum, vel per errorem intellectûs, vel per Diaboli persuasionem, sed per liberam potius electionem suam ac προαίρεσιν, ad eandem provolâsse, promoventibus dissidiorum negotium rivulis majoribus tribus ex pravitate Voluntatis emanantibus & Johanni Apostolo probè notatis, hôc locô, inverso ordine recensendis:
notes: Will-pravity prior; free προαίρεσις; three Johannine rivulets preview.
